entries.title: I Samuel 20:1
segments: This is a state of trial, and even obedience to God will not keep a person from sufferings; yet it will cause them to be overruled for his good and the good of others.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:5
segments: The new moon; the beginning of the month, when it was customary for relatives to unite in a sacrifice and a feast.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:10
segments: The certainty that David would be king did not render it unnecessary for him to use means to preserve his life; nor does the promise of God, to keep his children to the end, render unnecessary their own diligent prayers and efforts to persevere in faith and holiness.  It is through the use of appropriate means, and not without them, that the end will be accomplished.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:12
segments: Sounded; learned his state of mind.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:14
segments: The kindness--that I die not; it was common, when one began to reign, for him to put to death those who were supposed to have a claim to the throne.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:15
segments:
My house; his posterity. 
 
The conduct of parents may deeply affect not only their children, but their distant posterity, and each one should so act as shall attend to secure blessings to all who come after him, to the end of time.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:16
segments: Require it; take vengeance on either party, should they break this covenant.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:18
segments: Thy seat; at the family feast.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:19
segments: The stone Ezel; this was apparently a way-stone.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:22
segments: Hath sent thee away; in order to preserve his life.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:23
segments: An habitual conviction that the Lord is witness of all we do, that we shall stand before him in judgment, and be treated for eternity according to our works, tends to make us circumspect, upright, and faithful.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:26
segments: He is not clean; Saul thought that David was ceremonially unclean, and had kept away on that account.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:27
segments: An appearance of kindness may cover a murderous heart, and no crime is so abominable that a supremely selfish heart, under strong temptation, may not commit it.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:31
segments: Men in saying, I will, or, He shall, often speak as if events depended solely on themselves, whereas they depend on God; and men ought ever to feel, that if the Lord will, they shall live and do this or that.

entries.title: I Samuel 20:39
segments: Men often promote more benevolent objects, and accomplish greater good, than they are aware of; and all who faithfully do their duty, however humble their condition, when they see the results of their labors, will admire the grace of God, and be filled with gratitude and joy.
